methodological_rigor.justification: This multiomic longitudinal study of 30 PLWH with cancer in the phase 1 CITN-12 trial employs bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq, plasma cytokine profiling, flow cytometry, and in vitro HIV infection assays with pre-specified exploratory analysis. Timepoints are prospectively defined, modules derived via GSEA with Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and LASSO feature selection used for cytokine-module integration. Single-cell analyses (n=12-30 participants per timepoint) appropriately distinguish cell subsets. In vitro validation using TLR agonists with IFNAR neutralizing antibody controls confirms ISG pathways. Key limitations include the observational, non-randomized phase 1 design, small n at EOT (n=14), single-sex predominance (29/30 male), and absence of a randomized control arm. Deconvolution of cell-associated HIV DNA and unblinded data collection are acknowledged.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Pre-specified exploratory analysis embedded within a phase 1 non-randomized clinical trial, Oxford LoE 4. Clinical relevance is high: the identification of a preexisting ISGhi immune state in a subset of PLWH as a predictor of HIV reservoir reduction with pembrolizumab has direct implications for patient selection in future HIV cure trials. The demonstration that 9/14 PLWH with cancer showed HIV DNA decline associated with sustained ISG and myeloid antiviral module expression provides mechanistic insight into therapeutic HIV remission strategies, an area of significant unmet clinical need.

reporting_quality.justification: The study adheres to clinical trial reporting standards with full demographic and clinical data in Supplementary Data 1, pre-specified exploratory analysis design, and Benjamini-Hochberg correction for bulk RNA-seq. All antibody panels are provided in supplementary tables. RNA-seq raw data are stated to be deposited to GEO upon publication but no accession number is confirmed in the manuscript text. Sample availability per assay per timepoint is transparently listed. Limitations of non-blinding and batch correction for RNA-seq are acknowledged. The ClinicalTrials.gov registration is cited.

novelty_literature.justification: This study provides the first comprehensive multiomic characterization of the immune mechanisms underlying HIV reservoir reduction following anti-PD-1 therapy in PLWH with cancer. The identification of ISGhi vs. ISGlo immune phenotypes at baseline predicting HIV reservoir outcomes represents a novel stratification framework. The mapping of transcriptomic signatures across >1,000 public single-cell datasets via SCimilarity suggests these states reflect generalizable immune programs. The demonstration that sustained ISG activation in ISG+ monocyte subsets (cluster 2) correlates with HIV DNA decline adds mechanistic depth beyond prior reports.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is logically structured, with clear progression from rapid immune changes (24h) through sustained effects (EOT) and mechanistic validation. Figures effectively integrate transcriptomic, cytokine, and clinical HIV data. The multiomic approach is well described with appropriate caveats about sample size. Methods are detailed with software versions, statistical tests specified per analysis, and Supplementary Data organization for full transparency. Some density in the methods section may challenge non-specialist readers, but this is appropriate for the study type.

key_strengths: First comprehensive multiomic longitudinal characterization of HIV reservoir reduction mechanisms in PLWH with cancer receiving pembrolizumab, identifying ISGhi vs ISGlo immune phenotypes as predictive of reservoir outcomes
Prospective pre-specified exploratory design with four longitudinal timepoints and integration of bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq, cytokine profiling, flow cytometry, and in vitro validation
SCimilarity mapping of anti-PD-1-induced transcriptomic signatures across >1,000 public single-cell datasets demonstrating generalizability of ISGhi immune state across disease contexts
In vitro validation demonstrating that TLR agonists and IL-15 (IFN-dependent pathway) restrict HIV infection, supporting mechanistic link between ISG induction and reservoir reduction
key_concerns: Small sample size (n=30 total, n=14 at EOT) with heavy male predominance (29/30) limits statistical power and generalizability; no formal power calculation was performed
Observational phase 1 design without randomized control arm precludes causal attribution of reservoir reduction to anti-PD-1 therapy versus natural history or cancer treatment effects
scRNA-seq performed on only a subset of participants at each timepoint (n=8-12), limiting cellular resolution analyses; group 1/2 single-cell comparisons at baseline are particularly underpowered
chief_reviewer.rationale: This study provides important mechanistic insights into anti-PD-1 immunotherapy as an HIV cure strategy, with prespecified longitudinal multiomic analyses and biologically coherent findings across platforms. The small sample size and non-randomized design appropriately limit the tier to Tier 2 with minor revisions needed to address power and generalizability concerns.
